note: Root-cause investigation of Phase 12C's hypothesis, re-derived against the pinned llama.cpp source directly (not assumed). See summary.json for the final, checkpoint-confirmed conclusion.

layers_vector_ownership.construction_site: third_party/llama.cpp/src/llama-kv-cache.cpp: allocation loop, layers.push_back({il, k, v, k_stream, v_stream}) -- runs once at construction, one entry per KV-cache layer.
confirmed_readers: get_k/get_v (llama-kv-cache.cpp ~1285/1305) -- fresh ggml_view_4d over layers[ikv].k/.v, called every graph build (every llama_decode)
cpy_k/cpy_v (llama-kv-cache.cpp) -- writes the current token's K/V into layers[ikv].k/.v, called every graph build
state_write_data (llama-kv-cache.cpp:2145) -- reads layer.k_stream[cr.strm] fresh from the live layers vector on every state_write call
update()'s stream-copy and K-shift paths (llama-kv-cache.cpp ~884) -- read layer.k_stream/v_stream fresh from the live layers vector
layers_vector_ownership.conclusion: every reader re-resolves layers[ikv].k/.v/k_stream/v_stream fresh on every call -- no caching of the tensor pointer itself was found outside the layers vector.

ctxs_bufs_allocation_granularity.finding: Construction allocates ONE ggml_context + ONE ggml_backend_buffer_t PER DISTINCT buffer type (llama-kv-cache.cpp: 'ctx_for_buft' lambda, std::map<buft, ctx> ctx_map) -- ALL layers sharing a buft (e.g. all CPU-placed layers under kv_dev_override) share ONE physical backend buffer. A single relocated layer can therefore never free that shared buffer on its first move away from it (other layers still reference it).
ctxs_bufs_allocation_granularity.implication_for_relocate_layer: relocate_layer's destination is always a brand-new DEDICATED (single-layer) ctx+buf pair, appended to ctxs_bufs -- this makes the SECOND move of the SAME layer (away from its own now-dedicated buffer) the first point where a real, isolated free is even possible.

graph_rebuild_assumption.question: Is a completely new ggml_cgraph allocated every decode?
graph_rebuild_assumption.answer: Yes -- confirmed via llama-graph.cpp: mctx_cur->get_k(ctx0, il) is called fresh inside graph construction on every llama_decode call (build_attn and related call sites).
graph_rebuild_assumption.kv_views_recreated: Yes -- get_k/get_v build a fresh ggml_view_4d over the CURRENT layers[ikv].k/.v every decode; nothing about the view itself persists across decodes.
graph_rebuild_assumption.scheduler_reset_per_decode: ggml_backend_sched_reset(sched.get()) is called automatically inside llama_context::graph_reserve (llama-context.cpp:2370), and graph_reserve runs on every single decode call (confirmed via 'sched_reserve: reserving ...' log lines appearing on every decode in every probe run this phase) -- there is no separate public reset primitive to test beyond what already runs automatically.
graph_rebuild_assumption.ggml_backend_tensor_copy_synchronicity: Confirmed synchronous by reading ggml-backend.cpp:477-498: for a GPU-source/CPU-dest copy it calls ggml_backend_tensor_get, which calls buf->iface.get_tensor directly (the blocking variant, not get_tensor_async) -- ruled out as an async-completion race.

control_experiments.different_layer_A_then_B: PASS -- see raw_different_layer_control_135m.json. Two different layers, each relocated once (both first-moves, neither triggers a free), decode remains correct. No crash.
control_experiments.unique_tensor_naming: Did NOT change the outcome (tested and reverted) -- rules out tensor-name-keyed caching as the mechanism.
control_experiments.genuinely_new_tensor_object_per_relocati: Already the design (not a fix to test) -- every relocate_layer call creates a new ggml_tensor in a new ggml_context with a new ggml_backend_buffer_t. Confirmed via pointer capture (points A vs C in the repro2 reproducer): tensor_ptr, buffer_ptr, and data_ptr all differ after relocation #1.
control_experiments.explicit_llama_synchronize_before_reloca: Did NOT change the outcome (still crashes when old backing is freed).
control_experiments.settling_window_multiple_ordinary_decode: Tested (4 extra decode() calls between relocation #1 and relocation #2, matching what mode=roundtrip does) -- did NOT prevent the crash in the repro2 reproducer.

ground_truth_method: cb_eval-based tensor/buffer-pointer capture (used for diagnostics throughout this and the Phase 12C probe) was found to report STALE identity specifically after a layer's second relocation, even when the underlying decode output is provably correct (see poison_test.json). This is a real, reproducible measurement artifact of the capture mechanism used in this research probe -- its exact internal cause was not conclusively traced (candidate: some graph node inherits the persistent tensor's name via ggml_set_rows's in-place-style result, independent of the scheduler's own leaf-tensor accounting) and is reported as UNKNOWN rather than asserted. All CORRECTNESS claims in this phase rely on the poison test (real generation output), never on this pointer capture alone.
known_safe_statement: Old backing remains referenced somewhere in the Vulkan/backend execution path after rebind; releasing it makes a later graph operation observe a tensor whose expected buffer is no longer valid. The exact internal owner of that stale reference was not conclusively identified within this phase's budget -- it is NOT confirmed to be ggml_backend_sched's prev_node_backend_ids/prev_leaf_backend_ids arrays (reset already runs every decode, reasoned analysis suggests these self-correct), and it is NOT confirmed to be a Vulkan buffer-pool/suballocation reuse bug specifically (plausible but not instrumented/proven). This is reported as UNKNOWN, not as a scheduler bug, per the explicit instruction not to overclaim root cause.
non_determinism_disclosure: The release-triggered failure does not manifest identically in every call pattern: mode=repro2 (relocation #1 -> ONE decode -> relocation #2 -> decode) reliably crashes (GGML_ASSERT in one scenario, SIGSEGV in another, both real memory-safety failures); mode=roundtrip (relocation #1 -> decode -> 4 MORE decode steps -> relocation #2 -> decode) reliably completes without a visible crash across 4 repeated runs. This difference is NOT treated as evidence that roundtrip's pattern is safe -- non-deterministic-looking but call-pattern-deterministic behavior of this kind is the classic signature of a use-after-free/stale-reference bug, not proof of correctness. See release_failure.json.
